content:
Anna L.: Heads up — hitting a weird TS typing regression with the JS SDK when used in ESM edge apps (Vercel Edge). Errors about overload resolution + generics losing inference.

Mike T.: ugh, can you paste the error and a tiny repro?

Anna L.: pasting minimal repro:
```ts
// app/edge/route.ts (ESM, tsconfig module: 'esnext')
import { createRedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference';

const client = createRedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY });

// fails to infer generic on `client.generate`
const out = await client.generate({ model: 'gpt-4o', prompt: 'hi' });
```
TS error: "No overload expects 1 arguments, but overloads do exist that expect 2." and "Type parameter 'T' could not be inferred."

Sophia R.: I think we've seen this before — usually 2 culprits: (1) ESM/CJS interop changes how TS resolves declaration entry points (exports/types) and (2) we have overloaded signatures in the SDK that play nasty with default generics.

Mike T.: do you have a package.json for the app? is it "type": "module"? and which TS target/resolution?

Anna L.: yep module=esnext, target=es2022, moduleResolution=nodenext, package.json has "type":"module". Works fine at runtime, only compile-time TS errors.

Sophia R.: quick workaround: explicitly pass the generic so inference isn't needed:
```ts
const out = await client.generate<InferShape>({ model: 'gpt-4o', prompt: 'hi' });
```
Not ideal tho. Another workaround: set "skipLibCheck": true so the SDK d.ts oddities don't block users while we fix it.

Anna L.: skipLibCheck is a last resort — breaks our CI if we suggest it. Wanted to figure out root cause.

Mike T.: I dug into the SDK's index.d.ts. We have overloads like:
```ts
function generate<T>(opts: GenerateOpts<T>): Promise<GenResult<T>>;
function generate(opts: GenerateOpts<any>, cb: Callback): void;
```
When TS resolves from an ESM import that points to an exported .js that re-exports from lib/cjs/index.js, sometimes TS picks the wrong declaration entry (the CJS one) and overloads mismatch.

Sophia R.: exact. The fix path: ensure package.json "exports" has both ./package.json, ./types, ./index.js maps for import and require, and that types entry in package.json points to the ESM-compatible d.ts (we already ship only one d.ts but need exports map to prefer the ESM flow). Also check tsconfig in SDK build: "declaration": true, "emitDeclarationOnly": true, and use ncc/esbuild to preserve exports.

Anna L.: any immediate changes we can push to help edge customers?

Mike T.: short term: add a tiny usage doc snippet in the SDK readme for edge runtime (ESM) telling users to set tsconfig moduleResolution=nodenext and optionally import like:
```ts
import { createRedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference/esm';
```
We don't actually publish /esm entry yet but we can add an alias export in package.json to point to the same ESM build — quick fix for a patch release.

ci-bot: PR #2345 — patch: add esm export alias (checks pending) :github:

Anna L.: sweet. Also, types issue with unknown vs any — some of the SDK generic constraints use unknown which results in more casting for callers. Thoughts?

Sophia R.: we intentionally used unknown in a few spots to avoid hiding unsoundness, but we can add helper overloads with generic defaults that fall back to any for ergonomics. Eg:
```ts
// ergonomic overload
function generate(opts: GenerateOpts<any>): Promise<GenResult<any>>;
// strict generic overload
function generate<T>(opts: GenerateOpts<T>): Promise<GenResult<T>>;
```
That keeps the strictness for users who explicitly type, but gives decent inference for quickstarts.

Mike T.: +1. Also update examples (sample-apps) to show the explicit generic in TypeScript-heavy examples so users don't stumble. I can open the sample-apps PR referencing the new docs snippet.

Anna L.: action items: (1) Mike — add README snippet & sample-apps PR showing tsconfig + explicit generic note; (2) Sophia — add exports alias in SDK package.json + ensure types entry; (3) Mike/Sophia — add the ergonomic overloads and a small test that compiles against tsconfig nodedext/esnext combos.

Sophia R.: will do. I'll also add a release note about edge compatibility + TS settings.

Mike T.: ping me when PRs land, I'll run through a couple of public edge templates (Vercel/Lab) to validate.

Anna L.: thanks all. this was blocking a customer onboarding flow (they're on edge and use strict tsconfig). cc @mike for follow-up. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: Build failed on PR #2345 — error: missing "types" field in package.json for @redwood/inference (tsc error).

Anna L.: adding that to the checklist — Sophia, can you include types field in the next patch?

Sophia R.: yep adding now, will push a tiny fix and re-run CI.
